In 1859, a broke businessman declared himself Emperor of the United States. And San Francisco just went along with it.
Joshua Norton had lost his fortune trying to buy up all the rice in the city.
So he sent a letter to a newspaper, naming himself Emperor Norton the First. The paper printed it.
He wore a blue army uniform with gold epaulettes, and a tall hat with a feather.
He ordered Congress to shut down. Nobody listened.
But the city loved him. Restaurants fed him for free, and some shops accepted the money he printed himself.
When a police officer arrested him in 1867, the public was furious. The police chief let him go, and after that, officers saluted him in the street.
When his uniform wore out, the city government paid for a new one.
He even ordered a bridge built between San Francisco and Oakland. People laughed.
More than sixty years later, the Bay Bridge opened.
When he died in 1880, as many as thirty thousand people came to the funeral of the man who ruled nothing.
